problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -5 & 0 & 1 \\ 7 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $AB=BA={I}_{3}$
- $AC=CA={I}_{3}$
- $B={A}^{-1}$
worked_solution:
- First, we check whether $AB=BA={I}_{3}.$ Computing $AB$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne {I}_{3}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, statement I is false. As a result, $B\ne {A}^{-1}$ and statement III is false too.

- Now, we check whether $AC=CA={I}_{3}.$ Computing $AC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -5 & 0 & 1 \\ 7 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $CA$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}CA & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 1 \\ -5 & 0 & 1 \\ 7 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, statement II is true.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".
